statements.text: Simulation model predictions that plant communities will be resilient to losing many pollinator species have not been tested empirically, and the assumption that pollination efficacy is unaffected by interspecific competitor interactions embedded in those models has not been validated in the field.

statements.text: The role of syrphid flies as efficient pollinators remains controversial and poorly characterized due to a lack of comprehensive studies on Syrphidae, particularly regarding the mechanisms by which their morphological traits (pile density, body region) translate into actual pollination services across plant species.

statements.text: Whether phenological decoupling between plants and pollinators under climate warming will actually threaten population persistence for most species remains unresolved, as plants appear more likely to advance phenology than insects in response to springtime warming.

ungrounded_examples.statement: Whether species interaction networks are truly dynamic or static over time, and what the drivers and consequences of interaction turnover are, remains a knowledge gap because networks are typically constructed from temporally aggregated data that implicitly assume interactions are fixed.

This approach has advanced our understanding of communities, but it obscures the timescale at which interactions form (or dissolve) and the drivers and consequences of such dynamics. We address this knowledge gap by quantifying the within-season turnover of plant–pollinator interactions.
